stem: The contractor cut corners on the new health center, so the roof started leaking after the first typhoon. What does 'cut corners' mean in this sentence?
choices: changed the shape of the building
finished the work ahead of time
did the work cheaply and badly
answer: did the work cheaply and badly
hints: This is an idiom, so it does not mean cutting real corners off a building.
Look at the result after 'so': the roof leaked after the first typhoon. What kind of work leads to that?
Think about what a leaking new roof says about how the contractor built the center. Pick the choice that explains the leak.

solution.methodName: Read the idiom as a whole

steps.action: Spot the idiom: 'cut corners' cannot mean cutting the corners of a building.
steps.why: The word-for-word meaning does not explain a leaking roof, so the phrase must be an idiom.

steps.action: Read the result after 'so': the roof leaked after the first typhoon.
steps.why: 'So' shows the leak happened because of how the contractor worked.

steps.action: Ask what makes a new roof leak: poor work, cheap materials or skipped steps.
So 'cut corners' means 'to do something in the cheapest or easiest way, skipping proper steps'.
The answer is 'did the work cheaply and badly'.

trapNotes.changed the shape of the building: This reads the words literally. Changing the shape of the building would not explain why a new roof leaks.
trapNotes.finished the work ahead of time: Finishing early is not a problem by itself and does not explain the leak. Cutting corners may save time, but it means skipping proper steps.
trapNotes.asked for a bigger budget: Asking for more money is not the meaning, and the sentence says nothing about the budget.
